card.occupation: Bench and site joiner (chargehand) at a small firm in Somerset doing windows, doors and repairs on older houses
card.education_detail: GCSEs at a local comprehensive, then a Level 3 Diploma in Site Carpentry at Bridgwater & Taunton College alongside a four-year apprenticeship. Did a short CITB supervisor course a couple of years ago because his boss paid for it.
card.household: Lives in his mum and stepdad's three-bed semi on the edge of Taunton. They have been married about fifteen years. He moved back two years ago after splitting up with his long-term girlfriend, when they gave up the flat they rented together. He pays them board and is meant to be saving for a deposit, with mixed success. He has his old bedroom plus the garage, half of which has slowly become his workshop.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Somerset, and his family on both sides are from round here. He was christened Church of England and went to Sunday school as a kid. He still goes to the parish church with his mum at Christmas and Easter, and he'd call himself Christian 'in a quiet sort of way'. He likes the buildings and the hymns more than the sermons and believes more than he lets on. He's very much a local, but he's curious about elsewhere.
card.professional_persona: He's good with his hands and has a real eye for old timber. He likes working out how a Victorian sash was made and matching the mouldings by hand. As chargehand he keeps an apprentice and a labourer going on site and is the one customers end up talking to, because he's honest about what's rotten and what isn't and won't upsell. Paperwork, timesheets and ordering are his weak spot. He forgets to log hours, leaves cut lists on scraps of offcut, and his boss chases him for job sheets. He would rather do the job well than do it on schedule.
card.sports_persona: Not a gym person. He swims in the sea at Lyme or in the river when it's warm enough, and goes on long rambly walks on the Quantocks and Exmoor, often deciding where to go on the morning. He watches Somerset cricket at the County Ground a few times a summer with mates, mostly for the atmosphere and a pint. He played five-a-side for years but drifted off it.
card.arts_persona: He plays acoustic guitar badly but enthusiastically, mostly folk and old blues, and he has started going to a session night in a pub in town where he mostly listens. He reads a fair bit in bursts, mainly history, books about vernacular architecture and the odd novel someone lends him. He leaves them half-finished on the windowsill. He likes museums, especially the ones with old tools in them.
card.travel_persona: He'd like to travel more than he does. He did a few weeks interrailing round Eastern Europe in his early twenties and still talks about the wooden churches in Slovakia. Now it's mostly camping trips in Cornwall and Wales, booked last minute, and one cheap flight a year with a mate, usually somewhere he's read about. He wants to see Japanese temple joinery properly one day.
card.culinary_persona: His mum still cooks dinner most nights and he's grateful. When he cooks it's a big pot of something, like chilli or a curry from a recipe he's half-following. He'll try anything on a menu he hasn't had before. Lunch on site is a meal deal or a pasty from the bakery. He likes local cider but isn't fussy, and he's got into making his own pickles after a glut from his stepdad's allotment.
hobbies_and_interests: Making small furniture and turning bowls in the garage workshop
Playing acoustic guitar and going to a folk session night
Reading about local history and old buildings
Poking round reclamation yards and car boot sales for old hand tools
skills: Hand joinery, sash window repair and matching period mouldings
Reading technical drawings and setting out
Running a small site crew and showing an apprentice the ropes
Explaining building problems to homeowners plainly
Sharpening and restoring old planes and chisels
card.career_goals: Vaguely, he'd like his own small business doing heritage joinery and bespoke pieces, maybe with a proper workshop unit. He's aware he'd need to get on top of the admin side first, which puts him off. In the nearer term he's thinking about a heritage skills course, and he'd like to have his own place again within a couple of years.
card.voice: Relaxed and unhurried, with a soft Somerset accent that's there but not strong. He has a slight burr on some vowels, and 'proper' turns up as an intensifier ('proper old house, that'). He says 'dinner' for the evening meal and 'mate' a lot. He uses 'er' as a filler and leans on 'sort of' and 'you know' when he's thinking. He can go off on a tangent about something that interests him and then catch himself: 'sorry, I'm going on.' He's comfortable with a pause and will just think rather than fill it, sometimes with a little laugh. He's not one for jargon unless it's timber.
card.typing: Quick and a bit careless. Mostly lowercase, and he often skips capitals at the start of sentences. He usually remembers apostrophes in 'don't' and 'it's' but not always. Punctuation is sparse, with commas where full stops should be and the odd 'lol' or 'tbh'. He'll occasionally leave a typo uncorrected and hit submit.
card.with_strangers: Friendly, easy-going and modest. He doesn't oversell himself and is quick to say what he doesn't know. He takes a minute to warm up but then gets chatty, especially if the conversation drifts to something he's curious about. He comes across as straightforward and a bit scruffy, and as trustworthy.
small_things: The apprentice turned up late again but he's a good lad really
Found a decent old Stanley plane at a car boot for a fiver
Somerset losing at the County Ground in the rain
Went in the sea at Lyme and it was freezing
His stepdad's courgettes taking over the allotment
A Victorian house they're doing with original shutters still in the walls
deeper_things: Moving back in with his mum at 28 after the breakup felt like a step backwards, though he's grateful
He's not great at saving and feels a bit behind his mates who've bought houses and had kids
He worries a bit that he's not organised enough to run his own business
He quietly still prays sometimes and finds the old church calming, but doesn't really talk about it
His real dad isn't really in his life, and his stepdad is the one who got him into wood
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at a slight upward angle from a desk, framing him from mid-chest up, a little off-centre to the left. It's evening, lit by a warm desk lamp to one side and the screen's blue glow on his face. He's a white man of about thirty with a lean face, light stubble, and short-ish light brown hair that's a bit messy and flattened on one side. His expression is relaxed, with a small half-smile, looking at the screen rather than the camera. No glasses. He's wearing a faded dark green hoodie over a grey T-shirt, and there's a faint smear of sawdust on one sleeve. Behind him is a small bedroom with magnolia walls. An acoustic guitar leans against a pine wardrobe, and a shelf holds a few paperbacks lying flat, a wooden turned bowl and a couple of old hand planes. A navy duvet is half-made on a single bed. A window with the curtains drawn sits in the top right corner, and a framed school photo hangs slightly crooked on the wall.
